prompt:
Re-layout the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL cinder-bear bite sprite atlas with MUCH MORE TRANSPARENT SPACE. Preserve the same 16 bear poses, bear identity, anatomy, direction rows FRONT/LEFT/RIGHT/BACK and detailed crisp original pixel-art look. This is a layout repair, do not invent a different action or turn the rear view to front.

The current sprites nearly touch and neighboring silhouettes enter one another's rectangular crops. THE MAIN REPAIR IS TO MAKE EVERY BEAR ONLY SIXTY PERCENT OF ITS CURRENT SIZE RELATIVE TO THE ATLAS. Make a big square transparent RGBA canvas and center the 16 MINIATURE bears on a perfect 4x4 grid. The bears must look SMALL with very large transparent gaps, not fill the cells. Example on a 1024x1024 sheet: each bear fits inside a central rectangle no wider than 150px and no taller than 150px within its 256px cell, centered at x=128/384/640/896 and y=128/384/640/896. Thus at least 50px empty TRANSPARENT margin around each bear in ALL directions. Both whole bodies and loose fur tips must be fully separated from every neighboring rectangular frame. Do not crop the bears to make room. Do not put any scenery, shadows, background color, border, grid lines, labels or text into the empty spaces. Exactly sixteen complete bear sprites, four rows by four columns, no lost/extra sprites.

Row1 faces front toward bottom, row2 faces left, row3 faces right, row4 faces back away toward top. Keep each row's four action phases in original order, the original four-legged heavy bear, broad clawed paws/short muzzle/round ears/tiny tail and ash-brown/charcoal fur. The action remains LOW FORWARD BITE: draw back low, open lower jaw and lunge low/forward, snap low, recover. Never throw the muzzle upward in a roar and never rotate the back-row face toward the viewer. Strong emphasis: HUGE EMPTY GUTTERS and MINIATURE FIGURES. Preserve rich clear pixel detail, no blur and no resampling-looking halos.
